clue.text: Food! Change course, grabbing food, for example on the way back

indicators.note: grabbing means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: to veer is to change course

indicators.note: on the way back means the words food and for example are read backwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: A diner suddenly switches menu, grabbing a snack on the return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' reverses both food and for example together, giving GEBURG; the setter uses food twice, once as the definition and once in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatless patty in a bun is an item one eats, so the bare word for nourishment covers it.

clue.text: Ship's container

definitions.meaning: a receptacle such as a jug, bowl or bottle

explanation.surface: A boat's cargo box.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a boat and any receptacle for liquids, two separate dictionary senses.

clue.text: Manager managing to absorb the language

indicators.note: to absorb means the letters sit within the words Manager managing, held there

explanation.surface: A boss is running a course in order to pick up a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the tongue spoken in Germany and Austria, an example of a language.

clue.text: Wimp massaged legs, rubbing oils with no end of caution

indicators.note: massaged means the letters are worked over and rearranged
with no means a letter is taken away from the mixed pool
end of picks the final letter of caution

explanation.surface: A timid person has their legs massaged, rubbing in oils with care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'massaged' rearranges LEGS RUBBING OILS, and 'with no end of caution' takes out the N. A big girl's blouse is British slang for a feeble or cowardly man.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for a feeble, timid man, so it is a synonym of a weakling.

clue.text: Bitter, but relaxed about two points

indicators.note: about means the first piece is wrapped around the second

parts.note: restful means relaxed, calm
E and N are two compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: Someone is sour, yet laid-back about a couple of issues.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling aggrieved and harbouring a grudge is being sore or embittered, a close synonym.

clue.text: Crew needing altitude without hydrogen

indicators.note: without means the named element is dropped from the word for altitude

parts.note: height means altitude
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A team of people needs height but no hydrogen, as if launching a balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing boat with eight oarsmen, and the team rowing it, is named for its number of rowers.

clue.text: Language from jumper getting undressed

indicators.note: getting undressed means the outer letters, its clothing, are stripped off

parts.note: a jersey is a jumper, the British word for a knitted sweater

explanation.surface: A tongue taken from a pullover as someone strips off.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Itineraries must incorporate popular acts

indicators.note: must incorporate means the first piece takes the second into its body

parts.note: routes are itineraries, planned courses
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: Touring schedules must include well-liked performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Set performance pieces, as by comedians or dancers, are their acts.

clue.text: Green is bad — source of emotional charge!

indicators.note: bad means the letters are spoilt into a new order
source of takes the opening letter of emotional

explanation.surface: An exclamation that environmentalism is wrong, firing up strong feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge, as a battery, is to give it power, which matches invigorating or powering up.

clue.text: In transit, but approving hotel during depression

parts.note: passing means approving, as a bill or exam

indicators.note: during means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a trough is a depression, a low area
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller in transit gives a thumbs-up to a hotel in a low-lying valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone just stopping briefly on a journey is en route, the same idea as in transit.

clue.text: Bound to miss the end of autumn shoot

indicators.note: to miss means a letter is left out of the word for bound

parts.note: spring means bound, leap

indicators.note: the end of picks the final letter of autumn

explanation.surface: A leap that falls short at the end of autumn, a seasonal shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' means a young twig here, not firing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stem or twig with leaves is a young growth from a plant, a shoot.

clue.text: Uncontrollable urge isn't a mark of identification

indicators.note: uncontrollable means the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A compulsive urge is not a sign of who someone is.
explanation.definitionFit: A handwritten name is the personal mark that identifies the writer on a document.

clue.text: High spirits of auntie, perhaps going topless

indicators.note: going topless means the first letter, the top of a down light or the head of a word, is dropped

parts.note: an aunt is an example of a relation, a family member

explanation.surface: An aunt in high spirits goes topless, perhaps on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Great joy and exhilaration are high spirits, a synonym.

clue.text: Experiencing a pain on the right side of chest

indicators.note: right side of picks the last letter, the right-hand end, of chest

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: A sharp pain is felt on the right of someone's ribcage.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste something, such as freedom, is to experience it, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Exciting scenes from people who abseil?

definitions.meaning: suspenseful endings to episodes that leave viewers wanting more
climbers dangling from rock faces on ropes, read literally

explanation.surface: Thrilling moments come from rope climbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense episode endings are named after being left dangling over a precipice, and abseilers literally do that.

clue.text: Nasty accident — it's touch-and-go

parts.note: to hit is to touch or strike
to run is to go, operate

explanation.surface: A bad crash where it was a close-run thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A road collision where the driver flees the scene is a particular kind of nasty mishap.

clue.text: Attempts to box contrary to expectation will get testimonials

indicators.note: to box means the first piece encloses the second like a box

parts.note: tries are attempts
but introduces something contrary to expectation, meaning however

explanation.surface: A boxer's surprising attempts earn glowing praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Statements of praise and gratitude, such as farewell speeches, are testimonials.

clue.text: Risky to circumvent the Queen's court

indicators.note: to circumvent means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: chancy means risky
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: It is risky to sidestep a royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: A division of the English High Court that hears equity cases, an example of a court.

clue.text: Restore a Blairite? The changes!

indicators.note: changes means the letters undergo a reshuffle into new order

explanation.surface: Should a New Labour supporter be revived, given all that has changed?
explanation.walkthrough: A Blairite is a follower of Tony Blair, the British Labour prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To return someone to normal life or good health is to bring them back, a synonym of restore.

clue.text: Like some tyres artist set up

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for set is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: laid means set, placed

explanation.surface: A painter fits some car tyres.
explanation.definitionFit: Radial-ply tyres have cords running outward from the centre; the adjective describes them.

clue.text: Groups of fifty despatched by senior officer

indicators.note: despatched by means the senior officer gets rid of the fifty

parts.note: a general is a senior military officer
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Platoons of fifty soldiers are sent off by a commander.
explanation.definitionFit: In taxonomy these are the ranks grouping related species, so classes or groups.

clue.text: Throw a sickie — in bed, on holiday

parts.note: a bunk is a bed
off means away from work, on holiday

explanation.surface: Pretending to be ill and staying in bed while away on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: To throw a sickie is British and Australian slang for skipping work by feigning illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are British slang for skipping duty, so the slang idioms are synonyms.

clue.text: Estuary English ultimately suppressed by fail rate, oddly

indicators.note: suppressed by in a down clue means the following letter sits below the first piece
oddly picks the odd-placed letters of fail rate
ultimately picks the last letter of English

explanation.surface: Estuary English, a London-area accent, is kept down by a strange failure rate.
explanation.walkthrough: Estuary English is the accent of London and the Thames estuary; here 'Estuary' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A firth is a Scottish word for a narrow sea inlet or river mouth, an estuary.

clue.text: Managed returns merit recount

indicators.note: returns means the word for managed comes back, reversed

parts.note: ran means managed
to rate is to merit, deserve

explanation.surface: Management's returns call for a recount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recount' suggests counting votes again, but here it means tell.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to tell or relate it, a synonym.

clue.text: Reuters arranged to cover a king's finance officer

indicators.note: to cover means the rearranged news agency wraps around the a
arranged means the letters of Reuters are put in a new order

parts.note: R, rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: The news agency Reuters arranges to report on a monarch's money manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles REUTERS into TRESURE, which 'to cover' wraps around A.
explanation.definitionFit: The official in charge of an organisation's funds holds the purse, a finance officer.

clue.text: Join fool in backing European Union

indicators.note: in means the fool sits inside the other piece
backing means the abbreviation for European Union is turned around

parts.note: a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: A foolish person supports the European Union and signs up.
explanation.definitionFit: To join things together is to bring them into one, a synonym.

clue.text: Special Forces must cross east of enemy states

indicators.note: must cross means the special forces span around the letter

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, British special forces

indicators.note: east of in an across clue picks the rightmost letter of enemy

explanation.surface: Commandos must cross into hostile territory to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'states' looks like a noun (countries) but is the verb 'declares'.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to declare it, so the verb forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Fur needed if friend catches cold

indicators.note: catches means the friend holds the cold within

parts.note: china is cockney rhyming slang for mate, from china plate
a chill is a cold

explanation.surface: A fur coat is needed in case a pal catches a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: China means mate (friend) in cockney rhyming slang, from china plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft grey pelt of a South American rodent is a prized fur.
